report:
Model B appears domain-shifted toward culinary/food/restaurant/blog content.

Reasoning:
- Across the highest-norm cells (layers ~16–25, positions 1–4 especially), the logit-lens consistently points to cooking/food vocabulary: “restaurant,” “Restaurant,” “cooking,” “Cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “baking,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Baker,” “Cafe/Café,” “cook/cooked,” “Professional,” “Food.”
- It also surfaces blog/e‑commerce meta-tokens (“blog,” “blogger,” “blogging,” “www,” “No,” numerals, “International,” “Gift,” “Ads,” “Professional”), which fits food blogs, recipe pages, or product listings for kitchen/food items.
- Earlier layers show mixed nouns, but the strong, repeated culinary/blog signals dominate where the difference norm is largest (mid/late layers), indicating a high-level content bias rather than low-level tokenization effects.

Conclusion: B minus A strongly favors a cooking/food blog and kitchen/restaurant/product-listing style domain.
